page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The hybridisation
lines: In graphite every carbon atom is sp²
Each carbon is joined to three other
carbon atoms and carries no lone pair,
so it needs three hybrid orbitals.
One 2s orbital and two 2p orbitals mix
steps.why: Each carbon in graphite has only three bonded neighbours, so only three hybrid orbitals are needed. One s orbital and two p orbitals give those three, which is sp², and one 2p orbital is left unhybridised.
common_mistakes: Answering sp³ for graphite. That is the hybridisation in diamond, where each carbon is joined to four others.
Writing that all four valence electrons of carbon are used in sigma bonds. Only three are; the fourth is left in the unhybridised p orbital.
steps.memory_tip: Three bonded carbon atoms means three orbitals, so sp².
steps.margin_note: Answer sp² and say each carbon is joined to only three other carbon atoms.

steps.label: The sheets and the fourth electron
lines: The three sp² orbitals lie in one plane
at 120° to one another, so the carbon
atoms build flat sheets of hexagonal
The fourth valence electron of each
carbon stays in the unhybridised p
orbital and is delocalised over the

lines.text: Carbon in graphite is sp² hybridised

steps.why: Three sp² orbitals at 120° fill a plane with six-membered rings, which is why graphite is built of flat sheets. The p orbital left over on every carbon holds one electron, and those electrons spread over the sheet instead of staying between two atoms.
common_mistakes: Saying the sheets are puckered. Three sp² orbitals lie in one plane, so each sheet is flat.
Using the fourth electron to make a fourth sigma bond. Each carbon makes three sigma bonds only; the fourth electron is delocalised.
steps.memory_tip: Three neighbours means sp², a flat sheet and 120° angles.
steps.margin_note: Say what happens to the fourth electron; the hybridisation alone is not the whole answer.

insider_note: The answer itself is sp², so a complete answer says each carbon is joined to only three others in flat hexagonal sheets and that the fourth electron is left delocalised over the sheet.
